data.label: REPLAY
data.source: A recorded run, re-evaluated against your limits. Nothing is running on a GPU now.

narration.text: Replaying a recorded run of Granite 3.1 3B-A800M (earlier test, non-Meta) on one H100. Mixture-of-Experts decoding. Your limits: slowest 1% may get 10% slower, answers must agree at least 95%.

data.label: SAM 3.1 outlines 12 racks
data.inputs: a room photo or IR still

narration.text: SAM 3.1, Meta's segmentation model, outlines every rack in the room picture: 12 racks found. This is the example room: the picture is made up.

data.summary: SAM 3.1 outlines 12 racks
data.label: SIMULATED

narration.text: The heat inside each outline gives a temperature per rack. R-06 is the hottest at 43 °C; 2 racks at or above 35 °C. This is the example room: the picture is made up.

data.summary: Hottest rack R-06: 43 °C
data.label: SIMULATED

narration.text: Rack R-07 holds the H100 WattNot can read: its card draws 235 W at stock power (ESTIMATE). The other racks' power is not read by WattNot; those figures are examples.

data.summary: GPU power on 1 of 12 racks
data.outputs: watts for racks with a card
data.label: ESTIMATE

narration.text: Racks are ranked by heat. 1. R-06: Hottest rack in the room, but WattNot has no card access here (example rack), so it can only be watched. 2. R-07: Hot, and WattNot can read and cap the H100 in this rack.

data.summary: Hotspot ranking: R-06 43 °C, R-07 41 °C, R-08 33 °C
data.label: SIMULATED
Muse Spark picks: start with R-07

narration.text: Start with R-07. Hot, and WattNot can read and cap the H100 in this rack.

data.reason: R-07 is the hottest rack WattNot can act on. Hot, and WattNot can read and cap the H100 in this rack.
data.narration_note: Rule-based placeholder. A Muse Spark reply replaces this line when the run's event stream carries one.

data.summary: Muse Spark picks: start with R-07
data.label: SIMULATED
Set up the H100 host
data.inputs: a rented VM, the kit script

narration.text: A rented H100 machine is prepared with the model server and the measuring tools.

data.summary: Set up the H100 host
data.label: MEASURED
Write a grant: what may change, how far, for how long

narration.text: Before anything changes on the card, a short written grant says what is allowed: the power cap between 200 and 700 W and the server settings.

data.summary: Write a grant: what may change, how far, for how long
data.label: MEASURED
Approved: pre-approved by flag on the kit script (operator)

narration.text: A person had approved this grant in advance with a flag on the script. It was not clicked live.

data.summary: Approved: pre-approved by flag on the kit script (operator)
data.label: MEASURED
Probe: confirm the power meter works

narration.text: A short load confirms the card's own power meter is reading before any number is trusted.

data.summary: Probe: confirm the power meter works
data.label: MEASURED
Card found: H100 80GB, cap range 200 to 700 W

narration.text: The card reports itself: an H100 with 80 GB, and a power limit that can go from 200 to 700 W.

data.summary: Card found: H100 80GB, cap range 200 to 700 W
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: Granite 3.1 3B-A800M is loaded so that each router can be hooked. It normally uses 8 experts per token.

data.summary: Granite 3.1 3B-A800M loaded with transformers
data.label: MEASURED
Normal top-k: 3.23 J per token, p99 14.0 s

narration.text: With the normal 8 experts per token, each token costs 3.23 J and the slowest batch takes 14.0 s. This is what adaptive top-k is compared with.

data.summary: Normal top-k: 3.23 J per token, p99 14.0 s
data.label: MEASURED
Limits: agreement at least 95%, p99 up to +10%

narration.text: Your limits become checks: answers must agree at least 95% with normal top-k, and the slowest batch may be 10% slower.

data.summary: Limits: agreement at least 95%, p99 up to +10%
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: Normal top-k's own token choices are the reference. Adaptive top-k is scored by how often it would choose the same token.

data.summary: Reference: normal top-k's own choices
data.label: MEASURED
Routers hooked: keep experts until 90% of router weight is covered

narration.text: Each token keeps only as many experts as it needs to cover 90% of its router weight. Easy tokens use fewer; hard ones keep more.

data.summary: Routers hooked: keep experts until 90% of router weight is covered
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: Both versions ran 5 times. Normal top-k used 8 experts and 3.23 J per token; adaptive used 6.81 experts on average and 3.02 J per token, 6.4% less.

data.summary: Adaptive top-k: 3.02 J per token (normal 3.23)
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: Every token is compared with what normal top-k would say. Agreement is 94.53%. Your limit is 95%, so this does not pass.

data.summary: Agreement with normal top-k: 94.53% (your limit 95%)
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: The slowest batch took -10.9% as long as before. Your limit is +10%.

data.summary: Slowest batch -10.9% (your limit +10%)
data.label: MEASURED
Watch: 12.0 calls per task without the saver, 3.5 with it

narration.text: The saver reads the conversation before each call. Without a stop action the loop ran 12.0 calls per task; with the saver it ran 3.5.

data.summary: Watch: 12.0 calls per task without the saver, 3.5 with it
data.label: MEASURED
Detect: 24355 tokens per task without the saver, 5239 with it

narration.text: Repeated calls, no-op steps and plan cycles are flagged. Tokens per task fell from 24355 to 5239.

data.summary: Detect: 24355 tokens per task without the saver, 5239 with it
data.label: MEASURED
Nudge: 87.5% of tasks passed without the saver, 100.0% with it

narration.text: When the work looks done the loop is offered a done action. Tasks passed: 87.5% without the saver, 100.0% with it.

data.summary: Nudge: 87.5% of tasks passed without the saver, 100.0% with it
data.outputs: a done tool in the reply
data.label: MEASURED
Budget: 17.55 s per task without the saver, 2.92 s with it

narration.text: Step and token budgets cap the run. Wall time per task: 17.55 s without the saver, 2.92 s with it.

data.summary: Budget: 17.55 s per task without the saver, 2.92 s with it
data.label: MEASURED
Exit: the loop stops early (54.8 J, $0.0039 per task with the saver)

narration.text: The loop exits early with a reason: done. Energy per task about 54.8 J and cost about $0.0039 with the saver.

data.summary: Exit: the loop stops early (54.8 J, $0.0039 per task with the saver)
data.outputs: an early stop with a reason
data.label: ESTIMATE

narration.text: Adaptive top-k did not pass every gate, so there is nothing to approve. Normal top-k stays on.

data.summary: Nothing to approve
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: Not kept: agreement is under your limit. Normal top-k stays on.

data.summary: Adaptive top-k not kept
data.label: MEASURED
Before and after: 0.0% less energy per request

narration.text: The numbers go into one table: 0.0% less energy per request, p99 +0.0%. Water and cost are estimates; the energy is measured.

data.summary: Before and after: 0.0% less energy per request
data.label: MEASURED

narration.text: The room picture again. R-07 is acted on: its GPU power went from 235 W to 235 W, which is about the same, so the heat barely moves: this lever saves energy per token, not watts.

data.summary: Room heat map: R-07 41 to 41 °C
data.label: SIMULATED
Receipt rcpt_moe_a7b5b0dae89b: signed offline; no public log entry

data.summary: Receipt rcpt_moe_a7b5b0dae89b: signed offline; no public log entry

cooling.source: Uptime Institute, Global Data Center Survey 2024: industry-average PUE 1.56 (526 respondents)
cooling.formula: cooling and overhead energy = GPU energy x (PUE - 1)
cooling.caveat: An industry average, not this room's own PUE.

water.name: Data-center water use (WUE)
water.source: Headline WUE 0.36 L/kWh (on-site cooling), ESTIMATE, from LBNL 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (Dec 2024); up to 1.8 L/kWh including power-plant water (upper ESTIMATE); not measured
water.formula: litres = measured GPU kWh x 0.36 L/kWh (headline); up to x 1.8 L/kWh (upper, incl. power-plant water)
water.caveat: 0.36 L/kWh is on-site cooling water applied to GPU energy only (ESTIMATE); the 1.8 L/kWh upper also includes the water used to generate the electricity. A given site can be far lower or higher.

price.name: US commercial electricity price, 12 months to August 2026
price.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Monthly, Table 5.3 (released 2026-10-23): commercial rolling 12 months ending August 2026 = 13.87 cents/kWh

pipeline.title: Room scan
pipeline.desc: Finds the racks in a room photo or thermal still, reads their heat, checks it against GPU power and picks where to start.

subs.title: Segment the racks
subs.desc: SAM 3.1 (Meta) outlines every rack in the room photo or thermal still.
subs.inputs: a room photo or IR still

subs.title: Read each rack's heat
subs.desc: The thermal values inside each mask give a temperature per rack.

subs.title: Cross-check with GPU power
subs.desc: Where WattNot can read a card's power, it is set beside the rack's heat.
subs.outputs: power per rack we can read

subs.title: Rank the hotspots
subs.desc: Racks are ordered by temperature; a rack with no card access can only be watched.

subs.title: Muse Spark picks targets
subs.desc: Says in plain words which racks to start with and why.

pipeline.inputs: a room photo or IR still

used_for.meta: Room scan: Finds the racks in a room photo or thermal still, reads their heat, checks it against GPU power and picks where to start.
used_for.nvidia: Room scan: Finds the racks in a room photo or thermal still, reads their heat, checks it against GPU power and picks where to start.

pipeline.title: Baseline
pipeline.desc: The workload at stock power: energy per request and p99, before anything changes.

subs.title: Set up the host
subs.desc: The model server and the measuring tools go on the machine.

subs.title: Write the grant
subs.desc: A short file says what may change, how far and for how long.

subs.title: Approve it
subs.desc: A person approves the grant before anything on the card changes.

subs.title: Probe the power meter
subs.desc: A short load confirms the card's own meter is reading before any number is trusted.

subs.title: Find the card
subs.desc: NVML names the card and its allowed power range.

subs.title: Load the model with normal top-k
subs.desc: The model is loaded with its routers hooked but not yet changed.

subs.title: Measure normal top-k
subs.desc: Energy per token and p99 with the normal 8 experts per token.

used_for.e2e: Baseline: The workload at stock power: energy per request and p99, before anything changes.
used_for.nvidia: Baseline: The workload at stock power: energy per request and p99, before anything changes.

pipeline.title: Quality gate
pipeline.desc: Turns your limits into checks and proves the answer check works on the stock answers.

subs.title: Your limits become thresholds
subs.desc: The latency and quality limits you set turn into numbers a gate can check.

subs.title: Reference answers
subs.desc: Normal top-k's own choices are the reference that agreement is measured against.

used_for.oss: Quality gate: Turns your limits into checks and proves the answer check works on the stock answers.

pipeline.title: Adaptive top-k
pipeline.desc: Mixture-of-Experts models keep fewer experts per token; agreement with normal top-k is the quality check.

subs.title: Keep fewer experts
subs.desc: Each token keeps experts only until 90% of its router weight is covered.

subs.title: Run both versions
subs.desc: Normal and adaptive run the same rounds; energy and experts used are measured.

subs.title: Agreement with normal top-k
subs.desc: Every token is compared with what normal top-k would say.

subs.title: Latency check
subs.desc: The slowest batch against your limit.

used_for.hf: Adaptive top-k: Mixture-of-Experts models keep fewer experts per token; agreement with normal top-k is the quality check.
used_for.nvidia: Adaptive top-k: Mixture-of-Experts models keep fewer experts per token; agreement with normal top-k is the quality check.

pipeline.title: Agent waste
pipeline.desc: Stops the planning agent from calling tools it does not need. A done action, checks for repeated calls, no-op steps and plan cycles, and step and token budgets.

subs.title: Watch each step
subs.desc: Reads the conversation before each call (WasteGuard.before).

subs.title: Spot repeats, no-ops and cycles
subs.desc: Flags repeated calls, no-op steps and plan cycles (find_repeat).

subs.title: Offer the done action
subs.desc: Offers the done action the loop takes when the work is finished (done_tool_schema).
subs.outputs: a done tool in the reply

subs.title: Enforce step and token budgets
subs.desc: Stops the run when the step or token budget runs out (WasteGuard.before).

subs.title: Exit early with a reason
subs.desc: Ends the loop early and says why (WasteProxy.proxy).
subs.outputs: an early stop with a reason

pipeline.outputs: an early stop with a reason

used_for.meta: Agent waste: Stops the planning agent from calling tools it does not need. A done action, checks for repeated calls, no-op steps and plan cycles, and step and token budgets.

pipeline.title: Approve
pipeline.desc: Low-risk changes go through after the gates pass. A big one waits for an operator to click Approve. No answer in time means reject.

subs.title: Rate the risk
subs.desc: A small cap tweak near stock is low risk; anything bigger waits for a person.

subs.title: Operator check
subs.desc: A low-risk change goes through once the gates pass; a big one waits for an operator to click Approve.

subs.title: One-click undo
subs.desc: An applied change is put back with the token saved when it was applied.

used_for.oss: Approve: Low-risk changes go through after the gates pass. A big one waits for an operator to click Approve. No answer in time means reject.

pipeline.title: Keep or roll back
pipeline.desc: Keeps what passed every gate, rolls back what did not.

subs.title: Decide what to keep
subs.desc: Everything that passed all gates is kept; the rest is not.

subs.title: Apply it
subs.desc: The setting is applied to the card or the router.

subs.title: Roll back
subs.desc: Nothing qualified, or the run ended: everything goes back to stock.

used_for.nvidia: Keep or roll back: Keeps what passed every gate, rolls back what did not.

pipeline.title: Receipt
pipeline.desc: Writes the result down: numbers, labels, and the room before and after.

subs.title: Before and after, in numbers
subs.desc: Energy, p99 and quality before and after, in one table.

subs.title: Room heat map, before and after
subs.desc: The room picture again, with the racks that were acted on.

subs.title: Sign it
subs.desc: The receipt is signed with an offline key. Nothing goes to a public log.

used_for.sigstore: Receipt: Writes the result down: numbers, labels, and the room before and after.
